Today we discuss the most famous person who has ever lived. There are about two billion people in the world today who believe that Jesus is God. And so, a question then is: why is it that among many famous individuals in history—such as Alexander the Great, Julius Caesar, Socrates, Zoroaster, and Homer—it is Jesus that most people worship? So, what I want to do first is discuss the religion of Christianity. As you know, I grew up in Canada and studied the United States, so my entire life, Jesus was part of the culture and society. Growing up in Canada, not being Christian, I really didn't understand Christianity or its ideas.

First of all, it's important to remember that there are many denominations within Christianity, leading to a lot of disagreements. However, most Christians agree on several key points: first, Jesus is both the son of God and God himself; second, they believe he died for our sins because humans were expelled from the Garden of Eden due to disobedience; third, Jesus will return in what is known as the Second Coming, after his death, resurrection, and ascension to heaven. This will result in the last judgment where individuals are judged to either reign in heaven or burn in hell. Christianity is controversial because it asserts that believing in Jesus is essential for salvation, whereas other religious traditions emphasize being a good person.

Given this confusion around Christianity, why do so many people believe in Jesus? To answer this question, I will explain what we know for sure about Jesus based on scholarly research. This includes his birth around 4 BCE in Galilee (not the year zero as stated in the Bible), and that he was taught by John the Baptist, an apocalyptic preacher who preached that God would destroy evil people and offer a new life to those who repent before His return. At some point, Jesus began preaching a message different from his teacher's.
